timeline.body:
This PR changes policy manager/parser tests to rely on real files; this would solve the related CI failures already. 
But we need to remove assert for absolute/relative paths too, as that won't work with mixed windows/linux/mac policies like we already have on server (e.g. /proc/meminfo)

timeline.body: Why do we need to remove these asserts? We can specify absolute and relative paths in Windows. I don't think we should add leniency to make windows testing easier, let's adjust the tests so they aren't assuming `/` is the root path.

reply.body: It's in the description; the tests are fixed, but the asserts will fail anyway in production code because we have unix paths in policies with a cluster running on windows and vice-versa.

I think we can solve the eg `/proc/meminfo` in a different way: we don't need to add those to the policy on windows. Relaxing the assertions make it unclear why `path` and `relative_path` exist when there is no enforcement on what exists there.
Also, if for some reason we needed to support skipping certain file entitlements on different platforms in policy files, we could do that with an additional file property.

There will always be the matter of policy files; unless we add platform-specific sections to them, we may end up with a mix of absolute paths for different platforms.
I don't think we want that complication (platform-specific sections); if we do, we can address this separately.
